newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican businesses push construction bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexican businesses push construction bond plan.

text.p: Construction companies in the Mexican state of Nuevo Leon are promoting a project that would allow them to issue bonds backed by the government and financial institutions, said the president of the Nuevo Leon Construction Chamber, Hector Velasco.
"It's a pilot plan in the state of Nuevo Leon, then in other states, and why not, then at a national level," said Velasco in an interview with Reuters.
The new financing plan was put forward by E.F. Craven, a North Carolina-based construction company.
"It's a totally new concept to finance private-sector infrastructure projects, because it doesn't use public debt," said company president Charles Carson.
The plan would group or "pool" infrastructure projects to reduce risk and increase the possibility of the construction companies obtaining financing.
The plan foresees Mexican government organizations giving financial backing to the projects, possibly allowing the paper to be placed in international markets.

The projects could be backed by swaps for new bonds by existing Brady bonds, or with funds from institutional investors, foreign companies, or from Mexican companies interested in infrastructure projects.
Velasco said that various U.S.-based banks with interests in Mexico are looking at the project as other some large U.S. companies.
The construction group is meeting with various business groups in Mexico City to push the idea.
